tagline: A global leader in offshore wind installation, operations, and maintenance services
hero_kpi_rationale: The number of vessels is the primary operational and strategic driver for Cadeler, directly determining its ability to win offshore installation contracts and expand its presence in maintenance. The doubling of the fleet in 2025 is a strong signal of structural growth.

kpis.name: Fleet Size (vessels)
kpis.explanation: Total number of jack-up vessels for offshore wind installation.
kpis.description: In 2025, Cadeler increased from 5 to 10 vessels with deliveries of Wind Maker, Wind Pace, Wind Ally, Wind Mover and the acquisition of Wind Keeper.
kpis.signal: Fleet doubled in one year: operational capacity doubled.

kpis.name: Backlog
kpis.explanation: Total value of firm contracts and included options already signed.
kpis.description: The backlog reaches EUR 2.8B as of March 24, 2026, compared to EUR 2.3B at end 2024, supported by long-term contracts in installation and maintenance.
kpis.signal: Backlog at EUR 2.8B: strong financial visibility over multiple years.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Annual revenue generated from installation and maintenance activities.
kpis.description: Revenue increases from EUR 249M in 2024 to EUR 620M in 2025 driven by fleet expansion and strong vessel utilization.
kpis.signal: Growth of +149%: fleet expansion effect and strong vessel utilization.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Operating profit before depreciation and amortization, adjusted for non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA rises from EUR 126M in 2024 to EUR 425.4M in 2025, driven by scale effects and efficient cost management.
kpis.signal: Adjusted EBITDA increased 3.4x: significant improvement in profitability.

kpis.name: O&M Revenue Mix
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue derived from maintenance services.
kpis.description: In 2025, maintenance represents approximately one-fifth of total revenue, with the launch of Nexra, a platform dedicated to offshore wind after-sales services.
kpis.signal: 20% of revenue from O&M: strategic pivot towards recurring services.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.explanation: Total value of assets held by the company.
kpis.description: Total assets reach EUR 3.417B at end 2025, compared to EUR 1.7B in 2024, primarily due to vessels under construction.
kpis.signal: Assets up 76%: significant investment in fleet expansion.

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of 1.62 Bn € latest year

risks.title: Vessel unavailability and revenue loss
risks.score_rationale: Major risk placed at the beginning of Item 1A, highly intensive language ("material adverse impact", "loss of revenue", "liquidated damages"). Stable trend but recent incidents documented (Wind Scylla June 2025). Critical weight: limited fleet (9 operational vessels) makes each unavailability structurally impactful.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks and COSCO delivery delays
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly raised with geopolitical details (China-US tensions, Taiwan, potential sanctions). High uncertainty language ("continuing uncertainty", "could have an adverse effect"). Trend: up (designation of COSCO affiliates as military entities January 2025). Direct impact: 2 A-Class New Builds depend on COSCO, deliveries expected Q3 2026 and H1 2027.

risks.title: Demand volatility and dependence on offshore wind sector
risks.score_rationale: Major structural risk: lack of diversification (100% offshore wind revenue). Intensive language ("vulnerable", "volatile", "material adverse effect"). Trend: up (recent challenges documented: USA, Sweden, Netherlands, Germany, Denmark). Category weight: determines long-term fleet viability (25-year lifespan).

risks.title: Inherent operational risks of offshore operations
risks.score_rationale: Detailed operational risk with multiple concrete examples (accidents, storms, technical failures). Moderate but exhaustive language (listing of 10+ hazards). Stable trend but recurring incidents documented. Weight: insufficient insurance coverage (high deductibles, loss-of-hire not insured).

risks.title: Risk of backlog non-materialization
risks.score_rationale: Major contractual risk: backlog EUR 2,765M (Dec 31, 2025) but 374M in optional days (13.5%). Uncertainty language ("may not materialize", "subject to cancellation"). Trend: up (recent example: Ørsted LTA termination June 2025 for Hornsea 4). Weight: preliminary contracts increasingly common, difficult to convert.

risks.title: Fleet technical homogeneity and design flaws
risks.score_rationale: Fleet architecture-specific risk: "significant degree of operational homogeneity". Warning language ("possible that a technical or design failure... may be found to be similarly affecting... other vessels"). Stable trend but structurally inherent. Weight: a single defect could immobilize multiple vessels simultaneously.

risks.title: Contract execution risks and civil liability
risks.score_rationale: Detailed contractual risk: contracts impose strict specifications (vessel capabilities, installation precision, safety/environmental standards). Exposure language ("may be held liable", "consequential losses"). Stable trend. Weight: complex wind projects, narrow installation windows, multi-party coordination.

risks.title: Dependence on market reputation and customer relationships
risks.score_rationale: Qualitative risk: reputation and customer relationships are critical to securing contracts (e.g., A-Class New Builds pre-sold before delivery). Moderate language ("key factors", "adverse changes"). Stable trend but vulnerable to operational incidents. Weight: concentrated sector, major customers (Ørsted, etc.).

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence in the provided documents. Cadeler's strategy focuses on fleet expansion, offshore maintenance and operational safety, with no reference to AI or cognitive technologies.
